decision: Every authorization is scored inline before capture, with a rules-only fallback on timeout
why: Fraud caught before capture costs nothing; after capture it becomes a chargeback. The fallback means a slow model never approves blind.
alternative: Score asynchronously after capture and claw back.
value: 96% caught before capture while p95 stays under the 150 ms SLO.

decision: Rings are drawn as a device-and-card graph with pulsing hubs and dashed links
why: A ring is a shape: many cards converging on few devices and one address. A table of transactions hides it.
value: Analysts see the pattern in seconds and can explain it to others.

decision: p95 scoring latency is measured from the live stream, not reported by the model service
why: Latency is what the checkout experiences; computing it from events means chaos (DB pool saturation) shows up here the moment it happens.
value: The same number Tidewatch alerts on.

decision: The AI drafts a rule from the pattern; people save it in shadow mode first
why: A rule that blocks good customers is expensive; 7 days of shadow scoring shows its real hit rate before it acts.
alternative: Let the model auto-create blocking rules.
value: New rules ship quickly without surprise false positives.

decision: The authorization stream is the seeded world simulation, throttled to the screen
why: Dozens of events a minute per visitor would be real money on a hosted stream.
value: A believable stream at $0 that stays deterministic for tests.
